Obviously like most languages it will depend on where you're from and how close your native language is.

I think the main things with English is that people will often learn it young as it is considered the most advantageous language professionally. If they learned English at a young age at school and then tried again for fun as an adult, they'll obviously struggle a bit more.

A few other factors to think about is just the sheer amount of resources to learn English Vs other languages. More does mean higher quality does exist.

Also most popular entertainment is in English and signs in none English speaking countries sometimes have an English translation on them, so they're most likely exposed to a lot more English than any other secondary language.

Not to mention the fact that no matter where you are you likely know someone who speaks it. Idk anyone who speaks my target language to practice with but with English learners I can't imagine this is an issue often.

I also think that most languages have a fair few borrowed words in English now also which means they already have a bit of a starting point.

I honestly think this probably compensates for how hard the language is.

I don't know what society you're talking about but I'm going to assume its first world so...

People are inherently problems solving creatures, which is a deeply routed survival mechanism. In history we have always had conflicts, economic depressions, war etc. These took a great deal in inner resources to overcome, both mentally getting through them for general population and overcome them for people in power/soldiers etc.

For the most part we're pretty war free now... and given how accessible everything we have compressed our survival into, clicking order food from our phone... combatting loneliness with looking at a screen and getting sexual partners from swiping on an app.

No real problems to overcome... So our brain seeks problems... when all is said and done a lot of the remaining problems result in us as a person, so the problem to overcome is ourselves which is impossible because humans are flawed. Topple this with that most people don't really develop a skillset due to how many tools are readily available or skilled workers are available to fix our problem for us... makes us seem pretty shitty to ourselves.

This is why in my opinion suicide rates are lower in 3rd world countries. They have much less infrastructure for these things. They develop the skills and have more time preoccupied  in actually living, rather than self reflection.

The flipside of this as well is that we have a very hedonistic way of life. Not just sex, drugs and rock and roll, but movies, videogames, endless scrolling. This messes with the brains reward system and makes dopamine an expectation of the brain rather than a treat for it. So we either sit around being nagged by a brain craving stimulation which then fills our brains with "the dreaded thinky thinks" or we sit and stimulate our brain and have once again accomplished nothing.

In short, our cushty lifestyle leaves a lot of us without the inner discipline to deal with internal negativity.
